title: Primary 6 Area and Circumference of Circles
seo_title: P6 Area and Circumference of Circles Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE)
standard_text: Area and circumference of circle; area and perimeter of semicircle, quarter circle and composite figures
meta_desc: P6 circles practice for the PSLE: circumference, area, semicircles, quarter circles and composite figures. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Circumference = π × d. Area = π × r × r. Use the radius, not the diameter, for the area.
key_sub: Diameter 14 cm, π = 22/7: circumference = 22/7 × 14 = 44 cm; area = 22/7 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm².
body_html:
Circumference: the distance round a circle

The radius (r) goes from the centre to the edge. The diameter (d) goes across through the centre, so d = 2 × r. The circumference is the distance all the way round.

Circumference = π × d = 2 × π × r. The question tells you which value of π to use: 3.14 or 227. Use 227 when the radius or diameter is a multiple of 7.

Example 1

A circle has a diameter of 14 cm. Find its circumference. Take π = 227.

227 × 14 = 44

Answer: 44 cm

Area: π × r × r

Area of a circle = π × r × r (written πr²). Always use the radius. Area is in square units, such as cm² or m².

Example 2

A circle has a diameter of 20 cm. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.

r = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm. Area = 3.14 × 10 × 10 = 314

Answer: 314 cm²

Semicircles and quarter circles

A semicircle is half a circle. A quarter circle is a quarter of a circle. For the area, find the area of the whole circle, then halve it or divide it by 4. For the perimeter, add the curved edge and the straight edges.

Example 3

Find the perimeter of a semicircle with a diameter of 14 cm. Take π = 227.

Curved edge = 227 × 14 ÷ 2 = 22 cm. Perimeter = 22 + 14 = 36

Answer: 36 cm

Composite figures

Split the figure into shapes you know: squares, rectangles, circles, semicircles and quarter circles. For a shaded area, add the parts or subtract the part that is cut out. For a perimeter, trace the outline and add only the edges on the outside.

Example 4

Find the perimeter of the track above. Take π = 227.

2 semicircles = 1 circle: 227 × 70 = 220 m. Perimeter = 100 + 100 + 220 = 420

Answer: 420 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the diameter as the radiusHalve the diameter first: r = d ÷ 2
Working out r × 2 for r²r² means r × r: 5² = 25, not 10
Leaving out the straight edges of a semicirclePerimeter = curved edge + diameter
Writing cm for an areaArea is in cm² or m²; length is in cm or m
Using the wrong value of πUse the value the question gives: 3.14 or 227

faq.q: Are area and circumference of circles in the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. Circles are part of Measurement and Geometry in the P6 MOE syllabus, and PSLE papers often ask for the area and perimeter of figures made of circles, semicircles and quarter circles.

faq.q: Should my child use π = 3.14 or 22/7?
faq.a: Use the value the question gives. PSLE questions say “Take π = 3.14” or “Take π = 22/7”; 22/7 makes the working easier when the radius or diameter is a multiple of 7.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with circles in P6?
faq.a: Using the diameter in place of the radius in π × r × r. Another common mistake is leaving out the straight edges when finding the perimeter of a semicircle or quarter circle.

faq.q: How do I find the perimeter of a semicircle?
faq.a: Add the curved edge and the diameter. The curved edge is half the circumference: π × d ÷ 2.

items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge of the circle, so it is a radius.
The distance all the way round a circle is its circumference. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: Which of these gives the circumference of a circle with radius r?
items.e: The diameter is 2 × r, and circumference = π × diameter, so C = 2 × π × r. π × r × r is the area.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 8 cm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: 2 × 8 = 16 cm. 8 × 8 = 64 is not the diameter.
The line goes across the circle through the centre, so 18 cm is the diameter. Radius = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 25 cm. What is its radius?
items.e: Radius = diameter ÷ 2 = 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 5 m. Find its circumference. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: d = 2 × 5 = 10 m. C = π × d = 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 m. π × 5 alone gives only half the circumference.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 12 m. Find its circumference. Take π = 3.14.
A circle has a radius of 15 cm. Find its circumference. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: d = 2 × 15 = 30 cm. C = π × d = 3.14 × 30 = 94.2 cm. π × 15 alone gives only half the circumference.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 2.5 m. Find its circumference. Take π = 3.14.

items.e: C = π × d = 227 × 14 = 44 cm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 21 cm. Find its circumference. Take π = 227.
items.e: d = 2 × 21 = 42 cm. C = π × d = 227 × 42 = 132 cm. π × 21 alone gives only half the circumference.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 35 m. Find its circumference. Take π = 227.
items.e: C = π × d = 227 × 35 = 110 m.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3.5 cm. Find its circumference. Take π = 227.
items.e: d = 2 × 3.5 = 7 cm. C = π × d = 227 × 7 = 22 cm. π × 3.5 alone gives only half the circumference.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3.6 cm. Find its circumference, correct to 1 decimal place. Take π = 3.14.
The circumference of a circle is 62.8 cm. Find its diameter. Take π = 3.14.
The circumference of a circle is 88 cm. Find its radius. Take π = 227.
items.e: d = C ÷ π = 88 ÷ 227 = 88 × 722 = 28 cm. Radius = 28 ÷ 2 = 14 cm.

items.q: The circumference of a circle is 132 m. Find its diameter. Take π = 227.
items.e: d = C ÷ π = 132 × 722 = 42 m. 21 m is the radius.

items.q: Circle A has a radius of 6 cm. Circle B has a diameter of 10 cm. Which circle has the longer circumference?
items.e: Circle A has a diameter of 2 × 6 = 12 cm, which is more than 10 cm. The bigger the diameter, the longer the circumference. Circle A.

items.q: Which of these gives the area of a circle with radius r?
items.e: Area = π × r × r (πr²). r² means r × r, not r × 2. 2 × π × r is the circumference.

items.q: The radius of a circle is given in cm. In which unit is its area?
items.e: Area counts squares, so it is in square units: cm². The circumference is a length, in cm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 10 cm. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 3.14 × 10 × 10 = 314 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 5 m. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 78.5 m². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.
A = π × r × r = 3.14 × 8 × 8 = 200.96 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3 cm. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 3.14 × 3 × 3 = 28.26 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.
A = π × r × r = 3.14 × 9 × 9 = 254.34 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 20 cm. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 3.14 × 20 × 20 = 1256 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 1.5 m. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 3.14 × 1.5 × 1.5 = 7.065 m². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.
A = π × r × r = 227 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 14 m. Find its area. Take π = 227.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 227 × 14 × 14 = 616 m². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 21 cm. Find its area. Take π = 227.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 227 × 21 × 21 = 1386 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3.5 cm. Find its area. Take π = 227.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 227 × 3.5 × 3.5 = 38.5 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 35 cm. Find its area. Take π = 227.
items.e: A = π × r × r = 227 × 35 × 35 = 3850 cm². Do not work out r × 2 instead of r × r.
First find the radius: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm. A = 3.14 × 10 × 10 = 314 cm². Using the diameter as the radius gives 4 times too much.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 12 m. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: First find the radius: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m. A = 3.14 × 6 × 6 = 113.04 m². Using the diameter as the radius gives 4 times too much.
First find the radius: 56 ÷ 2 = 28 cm. A = 227 × 28 × 28 = 2464 cm². Using the diameter as the radius gives 4 times too much.

items.q: The area of a circle is 154 cm². Find its radius. Take π = 227.
items.e: r × r = 154 ÷ 227 = 154 × 722 = 49. 7 × 7 = 49, so r = 7 cm.

items.q: The area of a circle is 314 cm². Find its diameter. Take π = 3.14.
A circle has a radius of 4.5 cm. Find its area, correct to 1 decimal place. Take π = 3.14.
What makes up the perimeter of a semicircle?
c: the curved edge and the radius
the curved edge and the diameter
items.e: Go all the way round the semicircle: along the curved edge, then back along the straight edge. The perimeter is the curved edge and the diameter.

items.q: What makes up the perimeter of a quarter circle?
c: the curved edge and the diameter
items.e: A quarter circle has one curved edge and two straight edges. Each straight edge is a radius, so the perimeter is the curved edge and 2 radii.
r = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm. Area of the whole circle = 3.14 × 10 × 10 = 314. Half of it: 314 ÷ 2 = 157 cm².

items.q: A semicircle has a radius of 14 cm. Find its area. Take π = 227.
items.e: Area of the whole circle = 227 × 14 × 14 = 616. Half of it: 616 ÷ 2 = 308 cm².

items.q: A semicircle has a diameter of 7 m. Find its area. Take π = 227.
items.e: r = 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 m. Area of the whole circle = 227 × 3.5 × 3.5 = 38.5. Half of it: 38.5 ÷ 2 = 19.25 m².
Area of the whole circle = 3.14 × 10 × 10 = 314. A quarter: 314 ÷ 4 = 78.5 cm².

items.q: A quarter circle has a radius of 28 cm. Find its area. Take π = 227.
items.e: Area of the whole circle = 227 × 28 × 28 = 2464. A quarter: 2464 ÷ 4 = 616 cm².

items.q: A quarter circle has a radius of 6 m. Find its area. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: Area of the whole circle = 3.14 × 6 × 6 = 113.04. A quarter: 113.04 ÷ 4 = 28.26 m².
Curved edge = 3.14 × 20 ÷ 2 = 31.4 cm. Perimeter = 31.4 + 20 = 51.4 cm. Do not forget the straight edge.

items.q: A semicircle has a radius of 7 cm. Find its perimeter. Take π = 227.
items.e: d = 2 × 7 = 14 cm. Curved edge = 227 × 14 ÷ 2 = 22 cm. Perimeter = 22 + 14 = 36 cm. Do not forget the straight edge.

items.q: A semicircle has a diameter of 42 m. Find its perimeter. Take π = 227.
items.e: Curved edge = 227 × 42 ÷ 2 = 66 m. Perimeter = 66 + 42 = 108 m. Do not forget the straight edge.
d = 2 × 5 = 10 cm. Curved edge = 3.14 × 10 ÷ 2 = 15.7 cm. Perimeter = 15.7 + 10 = 25.7 cm. Do not forget the straight edge.
Curved edge = 227 × 28 ÷ 4 = 22 cm. Add the 2 radii: 22 + 14 + 14 = 50 cm.

items.q: A quarter circle has a radius of 10 m. Find its perimeter. Take π = 3.14.
A quarter circle has a radius of 21 cm. Find its perimeter. Take π = 227.
items.e: Curved edge = 227 × 42 ÷ 4 = 33 cm. Add the 2 radii: 33 + 21 + 21 = 75 cm.

items.q: A quarter circle has a radius of 8 cm. Find its perimeter. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: Curved edge = 3.14 × 16 ÷ 4 = 12.56 cm. Add the 2 radii: 12.56 + 8 + 8 = 28.56 cm.

items.q: Find the length of the curved edge of a semicircle with a diameter of 14 cm. Take π = 227.
items.e: Curved edge = half the circumference = 227 × 14 ÷ 2 = 22 cm. Only the curved edge is asked for, so do not add the diameter.
Whole circle = 227 × 14 × 14 = 616 cm². Three quarters: 616 ÷ 4 × 3 = 462 cm².

items.q: A three-quarter circle has a radius of 7 cm. Find its perimeter. Take π = 227.
items.e: Curved edge = 34 of the circumference = 34 × 44 = 33 cm. Add the 2 radii: 33 + 7 + 7 = 47 cm.

items.q: A semicircle and a quarter circle both have a radius of 10 cm. How much greater is the area of the semicircle? Take π = 3.14.
items.e: Semicircle = 314 ÷ 2 = 157 cm². Quarter circle = 314 ÷ 4 = 78.5 cm². Difference = 157 − 78.5 = 78.5 cm².

sets.title: Composite figures: squares, tracks and rings

items.e: Square = 10 × 10 = 100 cm². Quarter circle = 3.14 × 10 × 10 ÷ 4 = 78.5 cm². Shaded = 100 − 78.5 = 21.5 cm².
The shaded part has 2 sides of the square and the curved edge. Curved edge = 3.14 × 20 ÷ 4 = 15.7 cm. Perimeter = 10 + 10 + 15.7 = 35.7 cm.
The diameter of the circle is 14 cm, so r = 7 cm. Circle = 227 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm². Square = 14 × 14 = 196 cm². Shaded = 196 − 154 = 42 cm².
Each quarter circle has radius 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm. 4 quarters make 1 whole circle: 3.14 × 10 × 10 = 314 cm². Shaded = 400 − 314 = 86 cm².
The shaded part is bounded by 4 curved edges only. 4 quarter circles of radius 10 cm make the circumference of one circle: 3.14 × 20 = 62.8 cm.
Each quarter circle = 78.5 cm². Two quarter circles = 157 cm², which covers the shaded part twice and the rest of the square once. Shaded = 157 − 100 = 57 cm².
The shaded part is bounded by 2 curved edges. Each = 3.14 × 20 ÷ 4 = 15.7 cm. Perimeter = 15.7 + 15.7 = 31.4 cm.
The 2 semicircular ends make 1 whole circle: 227 × 70 = 220 m. Perimeter = 100 + 100 + 220 = 420 m. The dashed lines are not part of the perimeter.
Rectangle = 100 × 70 = 7000 m². The 2 semicircles make 1 circle of radius 35 m: 227 × 35 × 35 = 3850 m². Total = 7000 + 3850 = 10 850 m².
Curved edge = 3.14 × 40 ÷ 2 = 62.8 cm. Straight edges = 30 + 40 + 30 = 100 cm. Perimeter = 62.8 + 100 = 162.8 cm. The dashed line is inside the window, so do not count it.
Rectangle = 40 × 30 = 1200 cm². Semicircle: r = 20 cm, 3.14 × 20 × 20 ÷ 2 = 628 cm². Total = 1200 + 628 = 1828 cm².
Big circle = 227 × 14 × 14 = 616 cm². Small circle = 227 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm². Ring = 616 − 154 = 462 cm². Do not subtract the radii first.

items.q: The shaded ring is between two circles with the same centre, of radii 14 cm and 7 cm. Find the total length of both curved edges of the ring. Take π = 227.
items.e: Outer edge = 227 × 28 = 88 cm. Inner edge = 227 × 14 = 44 cm. Total = 88 + 44 = 132 cm.

items.q: A semicircle is cut out of a rectangle 28 cm by 14 cm. Find the area of the shaded part. Take π = 227.
items.e: Rectangle = 28 × 14 = 392 cm². Semicircle: r = 14 cm, 227 × 14 × 14 ÷ 2 = 308 cm². Shaded = 392 − 308 = 84 cm².
Each semicircle has a curved edge of 227 × 14 ÷ 2 = 22 cm. Perimeter = 14 + 14 + 22 + 22 = 72 cm. The dashed sides are inside the figure.
Square = 14 × 14 = 196 cm². 2 semicircles of radius 7 cm make 1 circle: 227 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm². Total = 196 + 154 = 350 cm².
Big semicircle: r = 14 cm, 227 × 14 × 14 ÷ 2 = 308 cm². Each small semicircle: r = 7 cm, 227 × 7 × 7 ÷ 2 = 77 cm². Shaded = 308 − 77 − 77 = 154 cm².
The shaded part has 3 curved edges and no straight edges. Big curved edge = 227 × 28 ÷ 2 = 44 cm. Each small one = 227 × 14 ÷ 2 = 22 cm. Perimeter = 44 + 22 + 22 = 88 cm.
The 2 ends make 1 whole circle: 3.14 × 50 = 157 m. Perimeter = 80 + 80 + 157 = 317 m.

items.q: The wheel of Ahmad’s bicycle has a diameter of 70 cm. How far does the bicycle move when the wheel makes 1 complete turn? Take π = 227.
items.e: In 1 turn, the bicycle moves the circumference of the wheel. C = 227 × 70 = 220 cm.

items.q: The wheel of Mei Ling’s scooter has a diameter of 70 cm. How many metres does the scooter move when the wheel makes 50 complete turns? Take π = 227.
items.e: 1 turn = 227 × 70 = 220 cm. 50 turns = 50 × 220 = 11 000 cm. 11 000 cm ÷ 100 = 110 m.

items.q: The wheels of Hafiz’s bicycle have a radius of 35 cm. He cycles 440 m along East Coast Park. How many complete turns does each wheel make? Take π = 227.
items.e: d = 70 cm, so 1 turn = 227 × 70 = 220 cm. 440 m = 44 000 cm. 44 000 ÷ 220 = 200 turns. Change m to cm before you divide.

items.q: A round table top has a diameter of 1.4 m. Find the area of the table top. Take π = 227.
items.e: r = 1.4 ÷ 2 = 0.7 m. A = 227 × 0.7 × 0.7 = 1.54 m².

items.q: Ali used 25 of a roll of ribbon to go round the edge of a round table with a diameter of 70 cm. How long was the roll of ribbon at first? Take π = 227.
items.e: Edge of the table = 227 × 70 = 220 cm. 2 units = 220 cm, 1 unit = 110 cm. 5 units = 5 × 110 = 550 cm.

items.q: A wire 132 cm long is cut into 2 pieces. The longer piece is twice as long as the shorter piece. The longer piece is bent to form a circle. Find the radius of the circle. Take π = 227.
items.e: 3 units = 132 cm, 1 unit = 44 cm. Longer piece = 2 × 44 = 88 cm = circumference. d = 88 ÷ 227 = 28 cm, so r = 28 ÷ 2 = 14 cm.

items.q: A circular pond has a radius of 14 m. A path 7 m wide goes round the pond. Find the area of the path. Take π = 227.
items.e: Outer radius = 14 + 7 = 21 m. Big circle = 227 × 21 × 21 = 1386 m². Pond = 227 × 14 × 14 = 616 m². Path = 1386 − 616 = 770 m².

items.q: Mr Tan puts a fence round a circular garden with a diameter of 21 m. The fencing costs $15 per metre. How much does the fencing cost? Take π = 227.
items.e: Length of fence = 227 × 21 = 66 m. Cost = 66 × $15 = $990.

items.q: A semicircular lawn has a diameter of 28 m. One packet of grass seed covers 50 m². How many packets does Mrs Lim need to cover the whole lawn? Take π = 227.
items.e: r = 14 m. Area = 227 × 14 × 14 ÷ 2 = 308 m². 308 ÷ 50 = 6.16, so 6 packets are not enough. She needs 7 packets.
The 2 ends make 1 circle: 227 × 63 = 198 m. 1 round = 85 + 85 + 198 = 368 m. 3 rounds = 3 × 368 = 1104 m.

items.q: Mdm Wong cuts the biggest possible circle from a square piece of cloth of side 42 cm. What area of cloth is left? Take π = 227.
items.e: The diameter of the circle is 42 cm, so r = 21 cm. Circle = 227 × 21 × 21 = 1386 cm². Square = 42 × 42 = 1764 cm². Left = 1764 − 1386 = 378 cm².

items.q: Two equal circles, as big as possible, are cut from a rectangular card 28 cm by 14 cm. What area of card is left? Take π = 227.
items.e: Each circle has a diameter of 14 cm, so r = 7 cm. 1 circle = 227 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm². Card = 28 × 14 = 392 cm². Left = 392 − 154 − 154 = 84 cm².

items.q: The minute hand of the school hall clock is 14 cm long. How far does its tip move from 7.00 am to 7.45 am? Take π = 227.
items.e: In 1 hour, the tip goes round once: 227 × 28 = 88 cm. 45 min is 34 of an hour: 34 × 88 = 66 cm.

items.q: Siti cuts a round cake with a diameter of 20 cm into 4 equal pieces. Find the perimeter of the top of one piece. Take π = 3.14.
items.e: Each piece is a quarter circle with radius 10 cm. Curved edge = 3.14 × 20 ÷ 4 = 15.7 cm. Perimeter = 15.7 + 10 + 10 = 35.7 cm.

items.q: The radius of Circle A is 3 times the radius of Circle B. The area of Circle B is 154 cm². Find the area of Circle A.
items.e: Area uses r × r. If the radius is 3 times as long, the area is 3 × 3 = 9 times as big. 9 × 154 = 1386 cm², not 3 × 154.

items.q: A wire 72 cm long is bent to form a semicircle, with no wire left over. Find the diameter of the semicircle. Take π = 227.
items.e: Let the diameter be 7 units. Curved edge = 227 × 7 units ÷ 2 = 11 units. Perimeter = 11 + 7 = 18 units = 72 cm, so 1 unit = 4 cm. Diameter = 7 × 4 = 28 cm.

items.q: Mr Rahman’s rectangular garden is 20 m by 14 m. A semicircular flower bed with a diameter of 14 m is along one short side. The rest of the garden is grass. Find the area of the grass. Take π = 227.
items.e: Garden = 20 × 14 = 280 m². Flower bed: r = 7 m, 227 × 7 × 7 ÷ 2 = 77 m². Grass = 280 − 77 = 203 m².

items.q: Priya used 27 of her ribbon to go round the edge of a circular photo frame with a diameter of 21 cm. She used half of the remaining ribbon for a card. How much ribbon did she have left? Take π = 227.
items.e: Frame = 227 × 21 = 66 cm = 2 units, so 1 unit = 33 cm. Remainder = 5 units = 165 cm. Half of it is left: 165 ÷ 2 = 82.5 cm.

items.q: A hawker centre has 12 round tables. Each table top has a diameter of 1 m. Find the total area of the 12 table tops. Take π = 3.14.
The wheels of Kumar’s bicycle have a diameter of 56 cm. How many complete turns does each wheel make when he cycles 1 km? Take π = 227.
items.e: 1 turn = 227 × 56 = 176 cm. 1 km = 100 000 cm. 100 000 ÷ 176 = 568.18…, so each wheel makes 568 complete turns.
